findings.claim: All five video.json receipts hash their current video-artifact.md bytes, but they omit a binding target. Under the documented generic binding precedence they therefore default to each topic's artifact.html. The generated module lock records all five video evidence bindings as current: false even though T17 separately interprets the hashes as video-artifact.md and passes. The evidence and authoritative lock are internally inconsistent.
findings.recommendation: Give each video.json receipt an explicit repo-relative reviewedPath naming its topic's video-artifact.md (or an equivalent schema-supported target), regenerate module.lock.json, and verify all five bindings resolve to video-artifact.md with current: true while retaining T17 liveness checks.

items.note: Resolved on cfc0e896220070138c463a8487252d4d0579f4b0. The helper generates a 48-bit random suffix, creates without pre-dropping, retries SQLSTATE 42P04 collisions, retains the owned name, and drops only that name. On isolated PostgreSQL 18.3, the shipped starter, completed schema, alternate schema and three negative variants left the pre-existing relational_design_lab marker row 42 intact and no generated database behind. A scratch-only forced first collision with pre-existing relational_design_lab_000000000000 left marker row 99 intact, selected a second generated name, passed 5/5 and removed only the generated database and ownership record.

Resolved on current bytes with behavioral rather than one-spelling metadata checks. A completed numeric(5,2)/CURRENT_TIMESTAMP/NOT NULL schema passed 5/5; an alternate suitable numeric(10,2), timestamptz DEFAULT now(), NOT NULL design also passed. Constant 2000-01-01 default, nullable enrolled_at and unscaled numeric variants each exited 1 with only task5EnrollmentDefaults failing. The test also verifies an omitted time is transaction-current, explicit null is rejected, 87.25 is exact, bounds hold and 87.255 cannot remain at three decimal places.

Resolved on current bytes. The prerequisite explicitly distinguishes sockets from TCP and probes psql with -h, -p and -d matching the pgJDBC host/port/database path; it explains PGUSER parity and custom values. An independent TCP probe to 127.0.0.1:55439 reached the same isolated PostgreSQL 18.3 server used by pgJDBC, and the lab passed over that path. Socket-directory PGHOST values are explicitly excluded by both instructions and helper validation.

Resolved on current bytes. Password files are now the primary documented path with Unix mode 600 and the Windows location; PGPASSWORD is secondary and carries PostgreSQL's process-environment warning plus throwaway-account guidance. Against a SCRAM-authenticated isolated PostgreSQL 18.3 server, psql and pgJDBC 42.7.14 both succeeded using only a worktree-local PGPASSFILE at mode 600, and the offline lab passed 5/5 without PGPASSWORD.
